phases.title: Construction
phases.summary: Lines, volumes, boxes, perspective and the basic mannequin.
phases.intro: Learn to think in 3D. This is the most important phase: once you understand volumes, bodies become much easier to draw.

phases.title: Heads and faces
phases.summary: Skulls, jaws, axes, eyes and head angles.
phases.intro: Even for very stylized characters, you need to understand the volume of the skull, the orientation of the head and where the features of the face sit.

phases.title: Body and movement
phases.summary: Torso in volumes, limbs, joints, anatomy and dynamic poses.
phases.intro: This is where the box method really pays off: you will learn to orient the torso and the pelvis, connect the parts of the body and build believable poses.

session.title: Warm-up
session.instructions: Warm up your strokes: lines, circles and ellipses.

session.title: Volumes
session.instructions: Boxes, cylinders and volumes in perspective.

session.title: Technical exercise
session.instructions: The technical exercise of the week. It changes every day.

session.title: Reference study
session.instructions: Study a manga reference or a photo.

weeks.title: Lines, shapes and precision
weeks.goal: Control your hand and draw simple shapes.

days.title: Straight lines
days.exercise: Draw straight lines of different lengths, each in a single stroke, moving from the shoulder as much as possible.

days.title: Circles and ellipses
days.exercise: Draw 30 circles and 20 ellipses, without using a compass.

days.title: Flat shapes
days.exercise: Draw squares, rectangles and triangles of different sizes.

days.title: Cubes
days.exercise: Draw cubes, first from the front, then tilted.

days.title: Still life
days.exercise: Mix all the shapes and draw a small still life made of cubes, spheres and cylinders.

tips: Start with light strokes, then strengthen only the useful lines.
Draw your shapes big enough to keep their construction under control.
For ellipses, go around the shape in one fluid gesture rather than in small hesitant strokes.
Don't erase every mistake right away: spot what doesn't work and correct it on top.

weeks.title: The box method and perspective
weeks.goal: Be able to imagine a volume turning in space.

days.title: Simple boxes
days.exercise: Draw 15 simple boxes, showing the three main directions of space.

days.title: Boxes from every side
days.exercise: Draw 10 boxes oriented differently: seen from above, from below and from the side.

days.title: Construction lines
days.exercise: Draw construction lines and extend the edges to check their direction.

days.title: Stretched boxes
days.exercise: Draw a series of longer, flatter and wider boxes.

days.title: Stacked boxes
days.exercise: Build a small assembly of stacked boxes, like building blocks.

lessons.title: How to draw a box correctly

steps.title: Start with one face
steps.text: Draw a square or a rectangle to define the front of your box. It doesn't need to be perfect.

steps.title: Add depth
steps.text: Draw edges coming out of the corners in a consistent direction. Their orientation shows how the box turns in space.

steps.title: Close the volume
steps.text: Add the remaining faces. You can draw the hidden edges with light strokes to understand the whole structure.

lessons.callout: Mistakes to avoid: edges that change direction for no reason, faces that don't meet, or boxes that look like flat shapes. Don't just draw the visible outline: imagine the full volume.

lessons.title: The big exercise: rotating boxes
lessons.intro: Draw 10 to 20 boxes per session, with a different orientation each time.
lessons.callout: Don't chase a perfect perspective with complicated vanishing points right away. Start by understanding how the faces change when the volume turns.

weeks.title: From geometric shapes to the human mannequin
weeks.goal: Turn a character into an assembly of simple volumes.

days.title: Basic volumes
days.exercise: Draw spheres, boxes and cylinders on their own.

days.title: Your first mannequin
days.exercise: Build a mannequin with a round head, a torso in volume, a box for the pelvis and simplified limbs.

days.title: Tilt the torso and the pelvis
days.exercise: Tilt the torso and the pelvis in different directions.

days.title: 10 mannequins
days.exercise: Create 10 mannequins with their arms and legs in varied poses.

days.title: Rebuild a reference
days.exercise: Observe a character reference, rebuild it with simple shapes, then hide the reference.

lessons.title: The method you'll use for all anatomy

steps.title: The rib cage
steps.text: Imagine an oval volume or a box with rounded corners. Its axis shows which way the chest faces. You can simplify it to suit the manga style you're aiming for.

steps.title: The pelvis
steps.text: Use a box that can tilt. Its front face shows the orientation of the pelvis. The hips and the legs must connect to this volume.

steps.title: Limbs and joints
steps.text: Use cylinders or tapered shapes for the segments of the limbs, and simple spheres for the shoulders, elbows, wrists, knees and ankles.

lessons.callout: The key principle: a character is a construction in volume before being a drawing of muscles, clothes or outlines.

days.title: Spheres and axes
days.exercise: Draw 10 spheres with a vertical axis and a horizontal axis.

days.title: Side plane and jaw
days.exercise: Add the side plane of the skull and the jaw to each sphere.

days.title: Front and profile
days.exercise: Build five heads from the front and five in profile.

days.title: Three-quarter views
days.exercise: Draw five heads in three-quarter view, then five seen from above or below.

days.title: One character, three angles
days.exercise: Draw the same character from three angles, using the same construction.

lessons.title: Building the head in five steps

steps.title: The skull
steps.text: Start with a sphere or an egg shape.

steps.title: The side plane
steps.text: Imagine a flattened face on the side of the skull. It helps you place the temple and the ear.

steps.title: The vertical axis
steps.text: It runs down the middle of the face and curves as the head turns.

steps.title: The eye line
steps.text: It follows the surface of the face. When the head tilts or turns, this axis changes too.

steps.title: The jaw
steps.text: Connect the sides of the skull to the chin with simple lines.

lessons.callout: Don't jump straight to the eyes, the hair and the final outline. First check that the head is correctly oriented.

weeks.title: Facial features
weeks.goal: Place the features on the volume of the face.

days.title: Pairs of eyes
days.exercise: Draw 10 pairs of eyes, varying their shape and spacing.

days.title: Noses and mouths
days.exercise: Study noses and mouths from several angles.

days.title: Ears, brows and hairline
days.exercise: Place the ears, the eyebrows and the hairline on constructed heads.

days.title: Six expressions
days.exercise: Draw six faces with different expressions.

days.title: Three characters
days.exercise: Draw three distinct characters by changing their jaw, eyes, hairstyle and proportions.

tips: The eyes follow the curve of the face: don't always draw them like two flat stickers.
The spacing between the eyes, their size and their tilt strongly change a character's identity.
The ears stay attached to the sides of the skull, even when the head turns.
Hair has an outer volume. Draw the overall shape of the hairstyle first, then separate the strands.
For expressions, work the eyebrows, eyelids, cheeks and mouth together, instead of only changing the mouth.

weeks.title: Difficult angles and consistency
weeks.goal: Stop depending on the front view alone.

days.title: Three-quarter heads
days.exercise: Draw six heads in three-quarter view.

days.title: Looking up and down
days.exercise: Draw heads looking up and looking down.

days.title: High and low angles
days.exercise: Work on faces seen from a slightly high angle and from a low angle.

days.title: Four emotions
days.exercise: Draw the same character with four emotions, keeping the shape of the skull.

days.title: Six orientations
days.exercise: Invent a character, then draw their head in six different orientations.

lessons.title: Coach's exercise: the rotation
lessons.intro: Imagine a small box inside the skull, as a guide to orient the head. Turn this guide, then place the features of the face on its surface.
lessons.callout: This exercise helps you understand difficult angles instead of memorizing a single recipe for the eyes or the jaw.

weeks.title: Torso and pelvis in volumes
weeks.goal: Understand the central structure of the body.

days.title: Rib cages
days.exercise: Draw 10 simplified rib cages, shaped like an egg or a rounded box.

days.title: Pelvis boxes
days.exercise: Draw 10 pelvises as boxes oriented differently.

days.title: Connect with the abdomen
days.exercise: Connect the two volumes with the abdomen, varying the tilts.

days.title: Turning torsos
days.exercise: Build torsos that turn, lean or arch.

days.title: Five full poses
days.exercise: Rebuild five full poses, starting only from the two big volumes of the body.

lessons.title: Essential exercise: turn the torso and the pelvis independently

steps.title: Neutral pose
steps.text: Stack the torso and the pelvis without any real twist. Check their relative sizes and the general axis of the body.

steps.title: Twist
steps.text: Turn the rib cage one way and the pelvis the other. The body must keep a coherent link between the two volumes.

steps.title: Tilt
steps.text: Lean both volumes, then adapt the spine and the shoulders. Watch how the center of gravity moves.

lessons.title: How to connect the volumes
bullets: The rib cage and the pelvis aren't two rigid rectangles: they are simplified volumes whose shapes you can vary.
The spine connects them and follows a curve.
The abdomen adapts to the distance, the tilt and the twist between the two volumes.
The shoulder line and the hip line are orientation guides. They aren't always parallel.
Draw the volumes as if they were transparent at first, then clean up the outlines once their orientation is right.
lessons.callout: The test: if you can tell which way the chest faces and which way the pelvis faces without adding a single muscle or piece of clothing, your construction is starting to work.

weeks.title: Arms, legs, hands and feet
weeks.goal: Build the limbs without drawing them as flat lines.

days.title: Arms in volumes
days.exercise: Draw arms with simple volumes, marking the shoulders, elbows and wrists.

days.title: Legs in volumes
days.exercise: Draw legs, locating the hips, knees and ankles.

days.title: Joints
days.exercise: Work on the joints and on the changes of direction of the limbs.

days.title: Hands and feet
days.exercise: Simplify the hands into a palm block with small cylinders for fingers; build the feet as wedge-shaped volumes.

days.title: Eight full mannequins
days.exercise: Draw eight full mannequin poses with limbs built in volumes.

lessons.title: The cylinder method
lessons.intro: A limb is built with volumes between the joints, not with two random parallel lines.

steps.title: Draw the axis
steps.text: Start with a line that shows the direction of the arm or the leg.

steps.title: Add the volume
steps.text: Place an ellipse at each end, then connect them. Vary the thickness according to the segment of the body.

steps.title: Connect the joints
steps.text: Use simple shapes for the shoulders, elbows and knees. Check the orientation of each segment before drawing the final outline.

lessons.title: Exercises for each part

steps.title: Arms
steps.text: Draw an upper arm and a forearm in ten orientations, then bend the elbow at different angles. Careful: the elbow, the wrist and the shoulder aren't interchangeable and don't connect the same way.

steps.title: Legs
steps.text: Build the thigh, the lower leg and the foot. Practice with sitting, standing, crouching and moving poses.

steps.title: Hands
steps.text: Start with a box for the palm. Add the fingers as simplified segments, respecting their length and direction. Work on open hands first, then fists, and finally more complex gestures.

steps.title: Feet
steps.text: Build a wedge-shaped volume before adding the toes. Check the heel, the sole and the orientation of the ankle.

lessons.callout: Don't look for muscles and tendons yet. First learn to place the volumes and the joints correctly.

weeks.title: Gesture, proportions and dynamic poses
weeks.goal: Go from a stiff mannequin to a living character.

days.title: Quick gestures
days.exercise: Do 10 quick gestures, 30 to 60 seconds each.

days.title: From gesture to mannequin
days.exercise: Turn five gestures into mannequins, with the torso and the pelvis in volumes.

days.title: Cylinders and joints
days.exercise: Draw five poses using cylinders and simple joints.

days.title: Foreshortening
days.exercise: Study foreshortening: an arm reaching toward you, a leg moving away, a view from above.

days.title: Three full poses
days.exercise: Draw three full poses from references, building each one from the gesture to the volumes.

lessons.title: Four tools to bring your poses to life

steps.title: The line of action
steps.text: Before any detail, draw a curve that expresses the overall movement. It keeps poses from being too straight and symmetrical.

steps.title: Opposing axes
steps.text: Tilt the shoulders and the pelvis differently to create a natural movement. They shouldn't both be horizontal all the time.

steps.title: Foreshortening
steps.text: An arm pointing at the viewer looks shorter because it goes into depth. Build it with the axis and the volumes rather than trusting its apparent length.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: Watch where the weight of the body sits and where it touches the ground. A pose must look like it can hold, or clearly show why the character is falling or jumping.
